::: {.callout-note appearance="simple" icon=false}
**Slides.** [Open the deck at this part](../../live/europeanisation-one-day.html#/part-1-the-claim-and-credibility){target="_blank"} in its own tab, or follow it on the [slides page](slides.qmd).
:::

Part 1 sets out why social science is argued about at all, the matrix that separates reproducing from replicating, and the robustness study of SCORE (Multi100; Aczel et al. 2026), in which five analysts reanalysed the claim on which the day works. It then reads the paper with what SCORE found when it tried to reproduce and to replicate it. The hands-on work comes at the end and runs into the first break, so that if your machine gives trouble you miss none of the talk.

## 1. The plan of the day

**On the slides.** The facilitator sets out the plan of the day and its two kinds of aim, what you will understand and what you will be able to do, and the slides say what you do not need. Open the folder of the workspace in your IDE while the facilitator talks; if your installation failed, open the deck in a tab instead and leave it to load.

[Open the deck](../../live/europeanisation-one-day.html){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"} [Open the browser lab](../../cases/europeanisation/lab.qmd){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

## 2. The credibility of social science

**On the slides.** Follow the talk on what social science is for, on false positives and forking paths, and on incentives and questionable research practices. It ends on the red-card study, in which twenty-nine teams analysed one dataset, with the estimates of the teams grouped by the response distribution that each team assumed, a grouping to keep in mind for the rest of the day.

## 3. The three Rs

**On the slides.** The word 'replication' names three operations, which the slides set out as a matrix of data against analysis. The slides then turn to repeatability and credibility, a quick check on the matrix in peer review, and the practices of open research.

## 4. The robustness study from the inside {#the-robustness-study-from-the-inside}

**On the slides.** The slides show what an analyst received, the paper in brief, the two tasks of the robustness study and how the results of the two tasks were put on a common scale. The slides end on a forest plot of the results of the five analysts, revealed one row at a time.

To go further: [SCORE](https://codemoreh.github.io/ar4ds/score.html) on the AR4DS site.

## 5. The paper and its record in SCORE

**On the slides.** The slides present the paper of the original author (OA): the claim as the analysts received it, the four framing scales, the model that the OA fitted, and Model 1 and Model 2, which put the robustness question inside the paper. The slides go on to the attempts to reproduce and to replicate the paper in the SCORE programme, and end on the five questions that the analysts of the robustness study asked in the free phase of the project.

## 6. The workspace and the deck

**On the slides.** The slides set the workspace, in which you work, beside the deck, which shows each step and carries the work if your installation fails, and say what the tools cannot do.

## 7. Task 1 – The setup check

[Open the deck at Task 1](../../live/europeanisation-one-day.html#/hands-on-1-get-yourself-running){.btn .btn-primary target="_blank"} [Open the browser lab at Task 1](../../cases/europeanisation/lab.qmd#task-1-setup){.btn .btn-outline-primary target="_blank"}

In the workspace, open its folder in your IDE, run `source("R/check_setup.R")` until it reports no failure, and render `index.qmd` once. The deck shows the same check on the slide of Hands-on 1, three cells that report the version of R, a panel of 270 rows, 27 countries and 10 years, and fixest; if your installation fails, run those cells in the deck or in the browser lab, and carry on there for the rest of the day. The warm-up that follows sorts four scenarios into the three Rs, in Task 1 of the report. The aim is to reach the point at which a line of R runs and the panel is in front of you, and if you need more time, carry on into the break.

**By the end of the part** R runs on your machine, you can tell apart the three operations that go under the word 'replication', and you have the claim and the results of the five analysts in front of you as the puzzle that the rest of the day works on.
